L-selectin is an adhesion molecule that binds to addressins on high endothelial venules, facilitating the extravasation process. analysis: Virgin T lymphocytes, also known as naive T cells, require specific surface molecules to extravasate into lymph nodes. The process involves the chemokine receptor CCR7 and the adhesion molecule L-selectin. CCR7 interacts with chemokines CCL19 and CCL21, which are present in the lymph nodes, guiding the T cells to these sites. L-selectin binds to addressins on high endothelial venules (HEVs), facilitating the entry of T cells into the lymph nodes. This mechanism is well-established in immunology, and the enhanced information supports this consensus. Other molecules listed, such as VCAM, ICAM-1, CCR9, and CCR4, are not primarily involved in the extravasation of virgin T lymphocytes to lymph nodes.
